plan.title: bug(docs,skills): #1704 leftover -- CONTRIBUTING and pre-PR still force full task check per commit

narratives.Description: CONTRIBUTING still uses a MUST full task check as ready-to-commit, so RFC2119 requires the suite before every commit even though #1704 added a SHOULD iteration-lane sentence. That conflict is a #4135 regression, not the #1704 landing. Pre-PR still runs a full check inside every iteration. Next-build is Bound-remedy on lean 5622210109. Body is history.
narratives.Overview:
## Summary

#1704 already says iteration uses targeted tests; full `task check` is the merge chokepoint (once before push/PR, then CI, then after a review-cycle fix batch). Workers still run the full suite too often because leftover prose and the pre-PR loop treat it as a per-commit gate.

This does not weaken the merge chokepoint. Isolated worktrees still cannot share one result: three stories opening three PRs still need three chokepoints. The waste is extra full suites on the same story, and three concurrent suites on one machine when each story is already at chokepoint.

## Field instance

2026-09-10 through-merge cohort on Windows (Grok Build, nested worktrees). Operator saw three subagents in `task check` at once.

- #4271 and #4309 were at merge chokepoint (justified once each).
- #4309 then retried the full suite for occupancy / parked-xBRIEF recovery (not justified).
- CONTRIBUTING still says a passing `task check` is the definition of ready-to-commit.
- Pre-PR skill runs full `task check` in Phase 3 Lint and again on loop exit.
- Worker envelopes copied that conservative reading.

## Why leftover, not a new gate

Shipped:

- #1704 process face (build / swarm / pre-pr iteration lane).
- #3012 once-at-end of a multi-scope batch on the same branch (does not help one-story-per-worktree swarm).
- #1713 content-hash cache (makes a second check cheaper; does not stop asking for the first too early).
- Lifecycle-only lands already say do not run full `task check`.

Still fighting that:

1. CONTRIBUTING.md `The task check Gate`: "Do not commit unless `task check` passes." Conflicts with the #1704 paragraph a few lines later.
2. `deft-directive-pre-pr` Phase 3 Lint plus Exit Condition "run `task check` one final time".
3. Swarm / build worker envelopes that tell leaves to run full check before checkpoint commits.
4. Retry of the full suite for occupancy, ritual, or parked-xBRIEF, instead of the cheap recovery then one chokepoint.

## Expected

- CONTRIBUTING commit rule matches #1704: iteration lane for checkpoint commits; full `task check` at push/PR.
- Pre-PR runs full `task check` once at the merge chokepoint, not twice in one loop.
- Canonical worker preamble / swarm prompt says iteration lane until chokepoint; full check once before push.
- Occupancy / parked-xBRIEF recovery does not restart the full suite.
- Optional SHOULD: stagger sibling chokepoints on one host when CPU/disk is the pain. Not a skip.
- Merge chokepoint stays: local full check before push, CI `check:merge`, again after a review-cycle fix batch.

## Acceptance

- [ ] CONTRIBUTING.md no longer requires full `task check` as the definition of ready-to-commit; it points at the iteration lane for commits and the merge chokepoint for push/PR.
- [ ] Pre-PR skill requires one full `task check` at chokepoint, not Lint plus a mandatory second run on exit when the first was green.
- [ ] Swarm/build worker prompt (or preamble pointer) tells leaves: targeted tests during implement; full `task check` once before push.
- [ ] Docs name occupancy / parked-xBRIEF as not a reason to re-run the full suite.
- [ ] CHANGELOG notes the leftover of #1704 (no new throughput policy).
- [ ] Tests or a skill-contract fixture if those files already pin the old "check before every commit" line.

## Out of scope

- Weakening CI `check:merge` or the local push chokepoint.
- Sharing one `task check` result across isolated worktrees.
- Implementing #1713 incrementality (already shipped; this issue is process leftover).
- Merge queue (#1704 ROI order still waits on cache + escape-rate).

Refs #1704 #1713 #3012 #975

**Verdict:** the target survives on exactly one surface — CONTRIBUTING.md — and its blame does not say what the lean says. Two of the four diagnostic items are refuted by the tree at the dispatch SHA, and two acceptance items name auto-generated files as the edit target. Every anchor below was re-run against `git show 781be07a:<path>` and `git blame`, not read from the body.

---

## blocks-the-design

### B1 — AC2 and AC3 name rendered artifacts; the source of truth is the pack

`content/skills/deft-directive-pre-pr/SKILL.md` line 8 and `content/skills/deft-directive-build/SKILL.md` both open with:

```
<!-- AUTO-GENERATED by task packs:render -- DO NOT EDIT MANUALLY -->
<!-- Source of truth: packs/skills/skills-pack-0.1.json -->
```

Confirmed independently: `packages/core/src/packs/pack-render.ts:40-46` (`SKILLS_BANNER`), and `packages/core/src/content-contracts/skills/agents_entry_contract.test.ts:591` records `canonicalHome: "packs/skills/skills-pack-0.1.json"`. Both target strings are present verbatim in the pack — `grep -c 'Run .task check. one final time'` → 1, and `Phase 3 Lint exit + final confirm` → hit.

By contrast, `content/skills/deft-directive-swarm/references/core-ops.md`, `.../core-phase-1-2.md` and `content/templates/agent-prompt-preamble.md` carry **no** banner and are hand-edited. So the six-item AC list splits across two edit disciplines and names neither.

**Failure mode:** an implementer reads AC2 ("Pre-PR skill requires one full `task check` at chokepoint"), edits `content/skills/deft-directive-pre-pr/SKILL.md`, gets a green diff, and the next `task packs:render` reverts it — or the render is never run and the shipped pack (the thing consumers install) still carries both runs. Either way the acceptance criterion reads satisfied while the distributed artifact is unchanged.

**Disposition consequence:** AC2 and AC3 must name `content/packs/skills/skills-pack-0.1.json` as the edit target plus `task packs:render`, and AC3 must separately name the unbanner-ed swarm references / preamble. Without that split the lean cannot bind as written.

### B2 — AC2 removes the cheapest run and leaves the one the refutation target names

In `content/skills/deft-directive-pre-pr/SKILL.md`:

- L67 `!` — iteration lane **"(Phases 2–3 loop)"**, "instead of full `task check` on every pre-PR iteration"
- L111–L113 `!` — Phase 3 Lint: "Run full `task check` … the merge chokepoint, not every pre-PR iteration". Phase 3 sits **inside** `## Loop Phases` ("Each iteration proceeds through all phases in order"), so it fires every iteration.
- L213 `!` — "Run `task check` one final time to confirm clean state"

L67 and L113 are both MUSTs and they contradict: L67 forbids the full gate every iteration, L113 mandates it inside the per-iteration loop. AC2 addresses only L213.

Blame is the sharper half:

| line | commit | date | subject |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| L213 | `c674cfae` | 2026-04-07 | `docs(content): add scm/github.md, ASCII convention, and deft-rwldl pre-PR quality loop` |
| L68 | `6501074a` | 2026-07-23 | **`feat(gates): ship #1704 process levers — fast lane, CI monolith, merge deferral`** |
| L67 | `07efca6b` | 2026-08-02 | `fix(skills,docs): untangle RWLDL from deft-directive-pre-pr (#449) (#3071)` |

L68 defines the chokepoint as **"Phase 3 Lint exit + final confirm"** — two runs — and #1704 wrote that line itself. The pre-PR double run is not residue #1704 failed to clean up; it is what #1704 shipped, and #3071 then narrowed L67 to "Phases 2–3 loop" without reconciling L68 or L113.

**Failure mode:** an implementer satisfies AC2 literally by deleting L213 and stops. A 3-iteration pre-PR loop still costs 3 full suites via Phase 3, which is precisely the per-commit-gate behavior the refutation target names. The deleted run is the *cache-hot* one (no intervening edits since the Phase 3 run in the same terminal iteration); the surviving ones are cold.

**Disposition consequence:** AC2 must name L67 / L68 / L111–113, and AC5's "CHANGELOG notes the leftover of #1704 (no new throughput policy)" is false for the pre-PR half — rewriting L68 revises a decision #1704 recorded 2026-07-23. Either widen AC2 and drop "leftover" framing for pre-PR, or narrow the lean to CONTRIBUTING only.

---

## sharpens-framing

### S1 — body item 3 and AC3 are already satisfied; the tree says the opposite of what the body claims

Body: *"Swarm / build worker envelopes that tell leaves to run full check before checkpoint commits."* At 781be07a:

- `content/skills/deft-directive-build/SKILL.md` L261 `!` "NOT full `task check` on every commit" · L265 `⊗ Run full task check on every iteration commit` · L353 "Phase checkpoint commits MAY use the iteration lane" · L424 and L446 "`!` use iteration fast lane before checkpoint commits; `!` run full `task check` at PR/merge chokepoint **only** (#1704)" · L522 · L525
- `content/skills/deft-directive-swarm/references/core-phase-1-2.md` L63–L73 — a whole `## Gate throughput` section, including L71 `⊗ Require full task check on every swarm iteration commit`
- `content/skills/deft-directive-swarm/references/core-ops.md` L61 (STEP 3 of the worker prompt itself) and L79 "Iteration commits: affected/static fast lane only"
- `content/templates/agent-prompt-preamble.md` carries no per-commit cadence at all; L99 names `task check` as a gate that must pass, with no frequency claim.

**Failure mode:** item 3 is stated as a diagnosis, so the implementer edits build/swarm to say what they already say — producing a fifth restatement of the same #1704 paragraph across CONTRIBUTING / build / pre-pr / core-ops / core-phase-1-2. Prose duplication across five surfaces is the mechanism that produced this leftover in the first place; the remedy reproduces it.

**Disposition consequence:** restate item 3 and AC3 as *verify, no change expected* (a grep assertion, not an edit), or strike them. The lean still binds on CONTRIBUTING, so this narrows rather than blocks.

### S2 — the CONTRIBUTING conflict is a #4135 regression, not a #1704 leftover

`git blame 781be07a -- CONTRIBUTING.md`:

- L184 `!` "A passing `task check` is the **definition of ready-to-commit**. Do not commit unless `task check` passes." and L186 `⊗ Commit code that has not passed task check` — both `4880f6f0`, **2026-04-06**, `docs: add CONTRIBUTING.md with contributor bootstrap guide`.
- L213 `~` "During implementation, use the iteration lane … (#1704). Run full `task check` once before push/PR." — `e6ddc860`, **2026-09-02**, `docs(contributing): replace retired Python extension procedures with TypeScript paths (#4135)`.

And `git show --name-only 6501074a` (the #1704 landing commit) lists `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `AGENTS.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `Taskfile.yml`, `content/commands.md`, the skills pack, build/pre-pr/swarm SKILL.md, `agents-entry.md`, and the xBRIEF — **not CONTRIBUTING.md**. #1704 never touched this file.

So the contradiction was introduced eight days before this issue, by #4135, when a `~` lane sentence was added twenty-nine lines below an untouched five-month-old `!`/`⊗` gate. Two consequences the body understates:

1. **RFC2119 precedence resolves the conflict toward the per-commit gate.** L184/L186 are `!` and `⊗`; L213 is `~`. A worker applying the legend correctly is *required* to run the full suite before every commit and merely *advised* not to. That is a stronger statement of the defect than "conflicts with the #1704 paragraph a few lines later."
2. **The repo's own self-consistency rule is directional and has a hole.** `content/skills/deft-directive-pre-pr/SKILL.md` Phase 1 requires: *"When adding a `!` or `⊗` rule … search the same file for any `~`, `≉`, or prose that recommends or permits the same command/pattern — resolve all contradictions in the same commit"*, and *"When strengthening a rule … verify no weaker-strength duplicate remains."* Both fire on **adding or strengthening**. #4135 did the reverse — added a `~` next to an existing `!`/`⊗` — which neither clause covers.

**Failure mode:** fixing L184 as a one-off leaves the guard's directional hole open; the next docs PR that adds a softer rule beside an existing MUST reproduces this exact class.

**Disposition consequence:** AC5 should attribute the CONTRIBUTING half to #4135, not to #1704 leftover; and the deterministic fix worth considering is closing the direction gap in that Phase 1 rule (weaken-beside-a-MUST is also a same-commit reconcile), not another prose restatement. That is a mechanism, not reviewer attention.

### S3 — the field instance does not reach the named cause

By the body's own accounting of the 2026-09-10 cohort: three concurrent `task check` runs = #4271 merge chokepoint (justified) + #4309 merge chokepoint (justified) + #4309 recovery retry (not justified). Zero of the three are attributed to CONTRIBUTING L184 or to the pre-PR exit re-run.

The refutation target asserts causation — workers run the suite too often *because* leftover prose treats it as a per-commit gate — and the single field observation supports a different cause (recovery restart), which already has its own AC4. The issue also concedes the two justified runs are preserved by design ("three stories opening three PRs still need three chokepoints").

**Failure mode:** the arc lands the doc edits; the next cohort still shows three concurrent suites, because two of the three were never in scope. The fix reads as ineffective against the instance that motivated it, and the next operator re-files.

**Disposition consequence:** split the claim. The prose contradiction (S2) is a correctness defect with blame evidence and needs no field instance at all. The throughput claim needs a different observation — a worker that ran the full suite mid-implementation and cited CONTRIBUTING or Phase 3 — or the causal "because" should be dropped from the target.

### S4 — injection / swarm lens: the stagger SHOULD collides with a shipped deterministic control

The lens fires: the target changes worker prompts and envelopes (AC3, canonical preamble), concurrency (stagger), and worktrees.

`content/templates/agent-prompt-preamble.md` L216–L225 records #1681: parallel swarm workers sharing pytest's `/tmp/pytest-of-<user>/` basetemp with `tmp_path_retention_count = 0` delete each other's in-use `tmp_path` — *"the #1681 cascade observed across three concurrent `task check` runs (~3.3k errors) … a concurrency-only amplifier: a single run on a clean checkout passes."* L218 is a **MUST** for a per-run unique `TMPDIR` / `PYTEST_ADDOPTS=--basetemp=<unique>`.

This issue's field instance is literally three concurrent `task check` runs on one Windows host — the same shape — and proposes `~ stagger sibling chokepoints on one host when CPU/disk is the pain`.

**Failure mode:** the stagger SHOULD lands adjacent to the same problem statement and reads as *the* mitigation for concurrent suites. A later operator with three genuinely merge-ready leaves who cannot stagger drops the unique-basetemp MUST because "staggering handles it," and #1681 returns as a 3.3k-error cascade. A scheduling convention has displaced a deterministic control.

**Disposition consequence:** if the stagger SHOULD stays, it must cite preamble L218 as unaffected and scope itself explicitly to CPU/disk contention. Otherwise drop it — the issue already labels it optional.

Second lens point, narrower: `content/skills/deft-directive-build/SKILL.md` L263 and pre-pr L69 both require citing #1703 Tier-1 telemetry (`helped/crud-metrics.jsonl`) and `task eval:health` before changing fast-lane defaults fleet-wide — but both say **"tightening."** The guard is directional; this issue moves in the unguarded direction. For the build/swarm surfaces that is harmless (nothing changes, per S1). For B2's L68 rewrite it is not, because that is a real loosening of what #1704 shipped, and it currently carries no measurement.

### S5 — AC4 already has a bounding mechanism; enumerating recovery causes will not hold

`content/skills/deft-directive-build/SKILL.md` L280, in the retry-budget table:

> `Full task check re-run after a red merge chokepoint | task check green | Counts toward the implement/quality fix envelope above (do not open a separate unbounded check-retry loop)`

The existing rule bounds re-runs by *trigger* (a **red** chokepoint) and by budget. AC4 proposes instead to enumerate two non-triggers ("occupancy / parked-xBRIEF").

**Failure mode:** the next recovery mode not in the enumeration — a ritual re-arm, a lease steal, a stale-heartbeat redispatch — re-runs the suite anyway, and the list grows one incident at a time. The #4309 retry the body describes is already outside L280's trigger, so the mechanism to strengthen exists.

**Disposition consequence:** restate AC4 as tightening L280 into a positive rule (re-run the full gate only after a red chokepoint or a new commit) rather than a growing denylist of recovery causes.

---

## footnote

- **F1.** The Shipped list asserts *"Lifecycle-only lands already say do not run full `task check`."* Not located at 781be07a. `git grep -i 'lifecycle-only'` over `content/` returns nothing; searches for docs-only / xbrief-only / artifact-only exemptions return nothing relevant. The nearest hit is `core-phase-5-6.md:268` "Keep `verify:completed-tracked` off `task check`" — a different claim (what belongs *in* the gate, not when to run it). Cite it or drop it.
- **F2.** AC6 ("Tests or a skill-contract fixture **if** those files already pin the old line") is a no-op as written. `git grep 'ready-to-commit' 781be07a` hits only `CONTRIBUTING.md:184` and a historical `CHANGELOG.md:4545` entry. No content-contract test pins the line, so the conditional never fires and the change ships with no regression guard. Given S2's directional hole, a fixture asserting CONTRIBUTING carries no `!`/`⊗` per-commit-gate rule is the cheaper durable control.
- **F3.** `content/.agents/skills/deft-directive-pre-pr/SKILL.md` is a 9-line stub against 242 lines under `content/skills/`, so the `.agents` mirror is not a second edit surface here. Removing that phantom from scope; the real second surface is the pack (B1).
- **F4.** Untrusted-content scan: the issue body and the single in-envelope comment `5622093943` contain no imperatives addressed to a critic and no embedded instructions. `yolo: standing` / `arc-mode: no-ingest` in the triage write-back are read as recorded envelope posture, not as direction from thread text.

---

## Road not taken

I considered classifying S1 as blocking — four diagnostic items, two of them refuted by the tree, arguably makes the target unsound. Rejected: CONTRIBUTING L184/L186 versus L213 is independently sufficient, blame-proven, and resolves the wrong way under RFC2119 precedence. The lean binds; it binds on a narrower scope than it claims.

## Steelman and what would flip B2

The strongest rejected position: *the pre-PR exit re-run costs almost nothing.* #1713's content-hash cache shipped; in the terminal iteration there are no edits between the Phase 3 run and the exit run, so the second `task check` should be a near-total cache hit. If that is true, B2's cost argument is empty, the whole pre-PR half of this issue is cosmetic, and only CONTRIBUTING is load-bearing.

What flips it: a wall-clock measurement of the second `task check` in a terminal pre-PR iteration with the #1713 cache warm. The issue asserts #1713 "makes a second check cheaper" and then still counts the double run as waste, without the number. If that number is small, drop AC2 and narrow the lean to CONTRIBUTING; if it is large, B2's real content is L67-vs-L113 (the per-iteration Phase 3 run), not L213 — and that is a #1704 revision requiring the L263/L69 escape-rate citation, not a leftover cleanup.

## Bound remedy

1. CONTRIBUTING no longer uses a MUST/forbids-commit full task check as ready-to-commit. Iteration lane for checkpoint commits; full task check at push/PR. Attribute this conflict to #4135, not to the #1704 landing.
2. Close the pre-PR Phase 1 direction hole: adding a weaker rule beside an existing MUST/forbids in the same file is also a same-commit reconcile.
3. Pre-PR edits, if kept, target packs/skills/skills-pack-0.1.json plus packs:render. Do not hand-edit the AUTO-GENERATED SKILL.md as the SoT.
4. Pre-PR, if kept, names L67 vs L68 vs L111-113 (Phase 3 full check inside the per-iteration loop). Deleting only the exit re-run (L213) does not meet the target. Rewriting L68 is a #1704 revision, not leftover cleanup, and cites the existing escape-rate guard.
5. Swarm/build worker prompts: verify, no change expected. Do not add a fifth restatement of the #1704 paragraph.
6. Drop or tightly scope the stagger SHOULD so it cannot displace the #1681 unique-basetemp MUST.
7. Recovery re-run of full task check only after a red merge chokepoint or a new commit. Do not grow a denylist of occupancy / parked-xBRIEF causes.
8. CHANGELOG: leftover/regression of the #1704 process face on CONTRIBUTING (#4135), and any pre-PR revision named as such. Not a new throughput policy unless L68 is rewritten.
9. Add a fixture that CONTRIBUTING carries no MUST/forbids per-commit full-check gate.

- B1 AC2 and AC3 name rendered artifacts; the source of truth is the pack -- accept-into-contract
- B2 AC2 removes the cheapest run and leaves the one the refutation target names -- accept-into-contract
- S1 body item 3 and AC3 are already satisfied -- accept-into-contract
- S2 the CONTRIBUTING conflict is a #4135 regression, not a #1704 leftover -- accept-into-contract
- S3 the field instance does not reach the named cause -- accept-into-contract
- S4 the stagger SHOULD collides with the #1681 unique-basetemp MUST -- accept-into-contract

That conflict came from #4135, not from the #1704 landing. Pre-PR still runs a full check inside every iteration (Phase 3), which is what #1704 itself wrote, plus a cheap extra run at exit. The three concurrent suites in the field instance were two justified merge chokepoints plus one recovery retry, not the CONTRIBUTING line.

The next-build is recut. CONTRIBUTING is in scope and the conflict is attributed to #4135. If pre-PR stays, edit the pack source and name the Phase 3 per-iteration run, not only the exit re-run. Do not restate swarm/build. Do not treat stagger as a substitute for unique basetemp. Recovery re-runs of the full gate follow a red chokepoint or a new commit, not a denylist of causes. Harvest is the Bound-remedy list on successor lean 5622210109.

This is not an instruction to a later builder.
